description: Fast-growing fruit crop widely grown in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Gujarat, Karnataka and Maharashtra, fruiting within 9-10 months of planting. Insect-borne viruses are the main threat, so healthy seedlings and early removal of sick plants matter more than sprays.
npk_split: Apply in six equal doses at two-month intervals starting from the second month after planting, with 10 kg FYM per plant at planting.

Leaf curl virus.name: Leaf Curl Virus
Leaf curl virus.description: Virus disease spread by whiteflies that curls and crinkles the leaves and stops growth. Infected plants set few or no fruits and there is no cure.
symptoms: Leaves curl downward and inward and crinkle
Veins become thick and dark green on the underside
Leaves turn leathery and brittle with twisted stalks
Stunted plant with few, small, misshapen fruits
Leaf curl virus.spread: Whiteflies carry the virus from infected papaya, tomato, tobacco and weed hosts to healthy plants; it is not spread by seed or touch.
Leaf curl virus.action: Uproot and destroy infected plants at once and control whiteflies on the remaining plants.

treatment.name: Uprooting and destruction of infected plants
treatment.notes: No spray cures a virus-infected plant; early removal protects the rest.

treatment.name: Seedlings raised under insect-proof net (40-50 mesh)
treatment.notes: Plant only healthy seedlings; keep the field away from tomato, chilli and tobacco.

treatment.name: Neem oil 1500 ppm
treatment.notes: Against whiteflies on the leaf underside, with yellow sticky traps in the field.

Mealybug.name: Papaya Mealybug
Mealybug.description: Sap-sucking insect covered in white wax that forms cottony clusters on leaves, stems and fruits. Heavy attacks cause leaf yellowing, fruit drop and can kill the plant.
symptoms: White cottony masses along the veins on the leaf underside, on stems and on fruits
Leaves crinkle, turn yellow and dry
Sticky honeydew with black sooty mould
Ants moving up and down the stem
Flowers and young fruits drop
Mealybug.spread: Crawlers are carried by wind, ants, tools, clothing and infested seedlings, and the pest also lives on weeds such as parthenium and on hibiscus.
Mealybug.action: Remove and destroy heavily infested parts and weeds and release the parasitoid Acerophagus papayae or spot-spray the colonies.

treatment.name: Acerophagus papayae (parasitoid wasp)
treatment.notes: The most effective control; do not spray insecticides where parasitoids have been released.

treatment.name: Fish oil rosin soap
treatment.notes: Drench the colonies directly; neem oil 1500 ppm 5 ml/L is an alternative.

treatment.name: Buprofezin 25 SC
treatment.notes: Spot spray on infested plants only if the attack is severe and no parasitoids have been released; only where the label lists your crop.

Mites.name: Mites
Mites.cause: Tetranychus urticae (red spider mite); also Polyphagotarsonemus latus (broad mite)
Mites.description: Tiny mites suck sap from the leaf underside and multiply fast in hot, dry weather. Leaves turn pale and dry, and fruit skin becomes rough and scarred.
symptoms: Fine yellow-white speckling on the upper leaf surface
Tiny red or pale moving dots and fine webbing on the underside
Leaves turn yellow-bronze, dry and fall
Young leaves narrow, stiff and claw-like when broad mite attacks (looks like virus)
Rough, brown, corky patches on fruit skin
Mites.spread: Mites move on wind, on workers' clothes and from plant to plant where leaves touch, building up quickly in dry, dusty conditions.
Mites.action: Wash the leaf undersides with a strong water spray and apply a miticide if speckling keeps spreading.

treatment.name: Wettable sulphur 80 WP
treatment.notes: Spray on the leaf underside in the cool hours; can scorch leaves in hot weather.

treatment.name: Spiromesifen 22.9 SC
treatment.notes: Papaya leaves scorch easily, so test on a few plants first; one spray per season, only where the label lists your crop.

treatment.name: Water spray on leaf undersides
treatment.notes: Knocks mites off and raises humidity; keep the crop free of dust and water stress.

Mosaic virus.name: Mosaic Virus
Mosaic virus.cause: Papaya mosaic virus (Potexvirus); most field mosaic in India is papaya ringspot virus (PRSV-P)
Mosaic virus.description: Virus disease that mottles young leaves in light and dark green and stunts the plant. In Indian fields most mosaic is caused by the aphid-borne ringspot virus, and there is no cure for either.
symptoms: Light green or yellow and dark green mosaic pattern on young leaves
Leaves puckered or blistered and smaller than normal
Stunted plant with a bunchy top
Few, small fruits
Mosaic virus.spread: Aphids carry the ringspot virus from plant to plant within seconds of feeding, and true papaya mosaic virus spreads in sap on hands and tools.
Mosaic virus.action: Uproot and destroy infected plants as soon as mosaic is seen, before the virus spreads to neighbours.

treatment.name: Uprooting and destruction of infected plants
treatment.notes: No spray cures a virus-infected plant; remove plants before flowering for the best effect.

treatment.name: Washing hands and tools after handling sick plants
treatment.notes: Use soap and water; work in healthy plants first.

treatment.name: Barrier rows of maize or sorghum around the field
treatment.notes: Sow before planting papaya so incoming aphids land and lose the virus on the barrier crop.

Ring spot virus.name: Ring Spot Virus
Ring spot virus.cause: Papaya ringspot virus type P (PRSV-P, Potyvirus)
Ring spot virus.description: The most destructive papaya disease in India, spread by aphids. Plants infected young stay stunted and give almost no marketable fruit, and there is no cure.
symptoms: Yellow mosaic and vein clearing on young leaves
Leaves become narrow and thread-like (shoe-string)
Dark green oily streaks on leaf stalks and the upper stem
Ring or C-shaped marks on fruits
Stunted plant with poor fruit set
Ring spot virus.spread: Winged aphids pick up the virus from infected papaya or cucurbit plants and pass it on within seconds of probing; it is not spread by seed.
Ring spot virus.action: Uproot and destroy infected plants as soon as symptoms appear and replant only with seedlings raised under insect-proof net.

treatment.name: Uprooting and destruction of infected plants
treatment.notes: Insecticides do not stop this virus because aphids pass it on before they die.

treatment.name: Barrier rows of maize or sorghum around the field
treatment.notes: Sow 2-3 weeks before planting papaya; do not grow cucurbits in or near the field.

treatment.name: Seedlings raised under insect-proof net (40-50 mesh)
treatment.notes: Plant so that young plants escape the peak aphid season; replace the whole crop after one fruiting cycle if infection is heavy.

Ring spot virus.vector: Aphids (Aphis gossypii, Myzus persicae, Aphis craccivora)

healthy.name: Healthy
healthy.description: The leaf shows no sign of disease, pest or deficiency. Keep checking young leaves every week, as virus symptoms show there first.
symptoms: Uniform green leaves without mosaic, curling or speckling
No white cottony insects or webbing on the underside
Normal growth of the crown
healthy.spread: Not applicable - no disease or pest detected.
healthy.action: Continue regular irrigation without waterlogging, bimonthly fertiliser doses and weekly scouting.
